means: The camera sits over the subject and looks down. Danbooru's standard high-angle tag.
does: You see the top of the head, the shoulders foreshorten, and the GROUND replaces the sky as the background. The figure reads as small, exposed and observed. It lands reliably - the shot_cam_angle high panel is unmistakably looking down onto the character with the pitch opened out behind him. Be aware it also widens the shot as a side effect: lifting the camera puts more floor in frame, so faces get smaller than you intended.
reach_for_it: when someone is losing - defeat, surveillance, grief, a body on the ground. Also for legibility, when you need to show where people are standing relative to each other.
used_in: shot.cam.angle high; three shots in films/last-light.json and one in films/chrono.json
example_base: 1boy, solo, male focus, short dark hair, plain jacket, standing, city street, daytime
read_it_as: Compare the SHADING, colour and line - not the pose or framing. Adding any clause re-rolls the model's conditioning, so composition moves between the two panels even at a fixed seed. An img2img pass from one fixed base image would isolate the tag properly; that is not built yet.
